sources.entry: Moonlight - GameStream client for PCs (Windows, Mac, Linux, and Steam Link). [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/moonlight-stream/moonlight-qt) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Moonlight PC is an open source desktop client for streaming games and desktops from NVIDIA GameStream or Sunshine hosts, built with Qt.
summary.what_it_does: Moonlight PC connects to an NVIDIA GameStream or Sunshine host and streams its display to a PC. It supports hardware-accelerated video decoding on Windows, Mac, and Linux, with H.264, HEVC, and AV1 codecs (AV1 requires Sunshine and a supported host GPU). Features listed include YUV 4:4:4 (Sunshine only), HDR streaming, 7.1 surround audio, 10-point multitouch (Sunshine only), and gamepad support with force feedback and motion controls for up to 16 players. It offers both pointer capture for games and direct mouse control for remote desktop, and can pass system-wide shortcuts like Alt+Tab to the host. The README also covers build instructions for Windows (MSVC), macOS, Linux, and Steam Link, including an embedded build option for single-purpose devices.
use_cases: stream PC games to another computer
remote desktop access to a home PC
play games on a laptop from a gaming PC
low-latency game streaming over a local network
stream games to Steam Link hardware
build a custom streaming client for an embedded device
how_to_run: Install Qt 6.11 SDK or later (Qt 5.12+ supported on Linux).
Run `git submodule update --init --recursive` from within moonlight-qt/.
On Windows and macOS, also run setup-deps.ps1 (Windows) or setup-deps.py (macOS).
Build from the command line with `qmake6 moonlight-qt.pro` then `make debug` or `make release`.
The binary is placed in app/moonlight.
Alternatively, open the project in Qt Creator; packaging scripts live in the scripts folder.
notable: Open source client for both NVIDIA GameStream and the Sunshine host server
Supports AV1, HEVC, and H.264 hardware-accelerated decoding on desktop platforms
Optional embedded build mode for single-purpose devices, with KMSDRM rendering for slow GPUs
Also available as Android and iOS mobile clients, per the README
Packaged for Windows, macOS, Snap, Flatpak, AppImage, Raspberry Pi, and Steam Link
caveats: Some features (YUV 4:4:4, multitouch) are only available with Sunshine hosts, and AV1 needs Sunshine and a supported host GPU.
Steam Link builds are limited to 1080p, 60 FPS, 40 Mbps, and no HDR on original hardware.
Windows builds require MSVC (MinGW not supported) and a Qt SDK; macOS/Windows also need extra setup scripts.
